note: Normal daily run, Friday 11 Sep 2026 ~07:02-07:45 SGT (one session after the 10 Sep catch-up run). Latest COMPLETED US session is Thu 10 Sep (NY currently Thu 19:02, just after that close). HK/SG closed 10 Sep too; JP/KR's own index data consolidates a session late (latest confirmed JP/KR bars are 9 Sep) -- not a holiday, just late-publishing data. Thursday 10 Sep was a hot-PPI risk-off day: August PPI was in-line on the closely-watched monthly headline (+0.4% m/m, matching consensus) but ran hot on annual/core terms (+5.4% y/y, ~0.1pt above consensus; core +0.3% m/m/+4.7% y/y, energy/diesel +24.1% m/m driving over a third of the gain) -- Fed hike odds for the Sep 15-16 FOMC jumped from roughly 60% to roughly 70% on CME FedWatch (dispersion 48-70% across trackers/times through the session). That real-yield repricing hit gold/silver miners hard even though the Hormuz safe-haven case did not break: SLV -5.30% to $57.50, GLD -1.73% to $396.36, GDX -3.46%, Barrick -6.99%, First Majestic -4.86%, Hecla -3.98% -- Kitco framed it as metals "trading as a rates-and-dollar market, not a clean safe-haven market" right now, compounding profit-taking after gold's push to 10-week highs; the technical picture is genuinely disputed (some coverage shows gold/silver closed below both 50- and 200-DMA with RSI ~29-31/oversold, a reversal read; other coverage frames it as a pullback before an expected Q4 rally). Oil kept spiking on a DISTINCT, escalating driver: Iran claimed strikes on 10 vessels overnight into 10 Sep, described in coverage as the largest wave of Hormuz shipping attacks since the war began, with the US retaliating under a new "tanker-for-tanker" policy -- Brent pushed toward $108-109 intraday, WTI past $103.88. The rare-earth basket (MP -5.49%, USAR -4%, REMX -5%, UUUU -6.32%, Lynas -2.71%) sold off on a THIRD, separate catalyst: reports a Trump-Xi summit could be scheduled in Washington later in September, perceived as reducing the "China-decoupling premium" -- this happened even as USA Rare Earth broke ground on a $1.2bn South Carolina facility the same day. Equities fell only modestly (S&P -0.58% to 7591.70, Russell 2000 -1.04%) but VIX spiked +8.38% to 17.84 -- a real vol/index divergence -- and CNN's live Fear&Greed fell further to 33/Fear (from 36 the prior reading) while crypto-specific Fear&Greed held at 69/Greed (up from 66), a widening sentiment divergence. DXY fell for a 4th straight session despite the higher hike odds, a genuine counter-signal not fully reconciled this run. US breadth: no fresher confirmed reading than Wed 9 Sep's baseline could be sourced this run (StockCharts/Barchart returned empty) -- given the VIX spike, further deterioration is likely but unverified, so the prior reading is carried with that caveat rather than guessed forward. Weekly EPFR/Lipper fund flows: no release fresher than the week ended 2 Sep has published; a search hit that looked like a week-ended-9-Sep figure was traced to a mis-dated 2025 article and excluded. Today's (11 Sep) US CPI print is the decisive next data point into the Sep 15-16 FOMC.

macro.narrative: Friday 11 Sep saw the S&P 500 close at 7656.98 (+0.86%), snapping a four-day losing streak on broad breadth (all 11 sectors, all Mag7 green) even as August CPI ran hot enough to push CME-implied odds of a 25bp hike at the 15-16 Sep FOMC to roughly 87-90%, versus ~60-70% before the print. Headline CPI was in-line at 3.4% y/y / 0.4% m/m, but core CPI's 0.3% m/m beat (vs 0.2% expected) is what moved rates markets, with 10Y yields pushing toward the mid-4.9%s, their highest since the mid-2000s, under hawkish Fed Chair Kevin Warsh (Jackson Hole, 28 Aug) who is openly at odds with the White House's push for lower rates. Oil eased Friday (Brent -2.98% to $104.42, WTI -2.43% to $99.99) as a technical pullback from Thursday's $108 Hormuz-war spike, even though the US-Iran naval/tanker conflict remains hot with no ceasefire in force. VIX's collapse off Thursday's spike (17.84 -> 15.84, -11.2%) reflects the market treating an in-line headline as a known, priced quantity rather than a fresh shock, but this is a fragile, single-session relief rally into a live FOMC decision. A separate, still-unresolved thread is China's rare-earth squeeze on MP Materials/USA Rare Earth ahead of the 24 Sep Trump-Xi summit, a genuine swing factor for the critical-minerals complex over the next two weeks. Breadth underneath the rally is narrower than the index move suggests: Nasdaq new lows (128) badly outnumbered new highs (38) over the week even as Friday's NYSE advance/decline ran roughly 2:1 bullish.

drivers: Oil's Hormuz-driven rally (Brent >$100) adds a fresh, genuine near-term inflation-expectations tailwind ahead of tomorrow's CPI print.
Rising real yields (10y at 4.857%, highest since Nov 2023) are a price headwind that partially offsets the breakeven support.
CPI due 11 Sep is the single most important near-term catalyst for the inflation-protection thesis specifically.
New Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish tone raises the stakes on tomorrow's print more than under a dovish-leaning chair.

calls.name: iShares iBoxx Investment Grade Corporate Bond ETF
drivers: Duration risk from the 10y's spike to 4.857% (highest since Nov 2023) is the dominant headwind, overwhelming any spread-stability support.
No credit-specific stress signal found this run -- the move is a pure rates story, not a spread-widening one.
Same CPI-tomorrow/FOMC-week two-sided setup as the rest of the Treasury/credit curve.
Corporate fundamentals remain a genuine support versus a real credit-stress scenario, which has not emerged.

calls.name: iShares iBoxx High Yield Corporate Bond ETF
drivers: Shorter effective duration than IG/Treasuries means less direct price impact from this week's yield spike.
Energy-sector HY issuers benefit directly from the Hormuz-driven oil rally given HY's typically higher energy weighting.
No credit-stress signal found this run -- spreads have not been reported widening alongside the equity/rates volatility.
Same CPI/FOMC-week catalysts as the rest of the credit complex.

calls.name: iShares JP Morgan USD Emerging Markets Bond ETF
drivers: Dollar strength (DXY ~99.5-99.7 post-Jackson Hole) is a direct headwind for USD-denominated EM debt via issuer funding costs.
Higher US rates (57-72% hike odds) generally tighten global dollar-funding conditions for EM sovereigns.
Oil-importing EM sovereigns face an added terms-of-trade headwind from the Hormuz-driven oil spike; oil exporters within the index benefit.
No EMB-specific fresh catalyst found this run; view is macro-inferred.

calls.name: Vanguard Total Bond Market ETF
drivers: Blended Treasury/IG-credit duration exposure means BND inherits the same hawkish-rate-repricing headwind as TLT/IEF/LQD, just diluted.
10y yield at 4.81% (highest since Jan 2025) is the dominant driver of the near-term price headwind.
IG credit-spread resilience (78bp, tight and stable) provides a partial offset versus a pure-duration play.
Softening labor data (JOLTS, ISM Manufacturing) into Friday's NFP is the key swing factor that could reverse the rate-repricing headwind.
